# Hearth

> Family location sharing you host yourself. Free and open source under the
> AGPL-3.0 (github.com/Qureshi-DH/hearth). An iOS and Android app talks to an
> API server you run with Docker next to Postgres. There is no Hearth company
> server, no account with the project, no analytics and no ads.

Hearth is for families who want what commercial family locator apps do,
without their positions living on a company's servers. It shows everyone in a
circle on a live map, tells the family when somebody arrives at or leaves a
place, raises an SOS, detects crashes, and records trips.

Status: the server is ready to run. The iOS and Android apps are built and in
App Store and Play Store review, and until they are out people build the app
themselves. It has not had an independent security audit.

## What it does

- Live map of everyone in a circle, with battery and whether they are walking
  or driving. The server asks each phone where it is every few minutes, and Live
  follows one person a fix a second while somebody watches.
- Places: arrival and departure alerts per place and per person, with quiet hours
- SOS that reaches the whole circle, and one-tap check-ins
- Optional crash detection from the phone's own sensors. It asks first, and
  only silence raises the alarm
- Trips with distance, duration and top speed
- Sharing set per circle: precise, approximate (a 750 metre grid) or paused
- Export your data, erase your history, or delete your account from the app

## Install

One command on a Linux machine with Docker:
`curl -fsSL https://qureshi-dh.github.io/hearth/install.sh | sh`

Container image: `dhqureshi/hearth-api` on Docker Hub, amd64 and arm64.
Needs Postgres 14 or newer.
